policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads the name 'Jeziel', which renders the qere ויזיאל (yod before the final aleph); the ketiv ויזואל would give a form with waw ('Jezuel/Jeziuel'). The English spelling distinguishes the qere.
ASV reads 'the Haruphite', with u vowel and pe, rendering the qere החרופי; the ketiv החריפי would yield 'Hariphite'. The English gentilic distinguishes the qere.

ASV 'when it had overflowed all its banks' translates the plural noun with third masculine singular suffix; qere גדותיו and ketiv גדיתיו differ only in the orthography of that same word ('its banks') and produce identical English. No ASV note is mapped here, so the base fallback carries the projection.

ASV text reads 'chief of the thirty', rendering the ketiv השלושים ('the thirty'); the qere השלישים would give 'the captains/officers'. The mapped textual_variant note, 'Another reading is, captains,' confirms that the ASV translators placed the qere reading in the margin and the ketiv in the text.
